title: Climate stability drives multidimensional nestedness of amphibian assemblages in a Chinese sky island system
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

The nested subset pattern (nestedness) has been widely used to explain species distributions in island and fragmented systems. Mountain sky islands serve as critical natural laboratories for understanding the evolutionary consequences of geographic isolation and climate change, but their species distribution patterns remain poorly understood. Compared to lowland fragmented habitat islands, biodiversity patterns in mountainous regions are more complex, and traditional drivers may not adequately explain the nestedness of sky islands. To uncover the underlying mechanisms of mountain biodiversity, this study sampled amphibians across 30 sky islands in the Dabie Mountains, China, aiming to explore the nestedness of amphibian assemblages and its formative mechanisms from taxonomic, functional and phylogenetic perspectives. Taxonomic nestedness was quantified by constructing species incidence matrices and calculating nestedness metrics, while functional and phylogenetic nestedness were assessed by integrating species similarities in ecological traits and phylogenetic relationships. Seven sky island characteristics and eight amphibian species traits were then selected as predictors of nestedness. Results showed that amphibian assemblages in the Dabie Mountains exhibited significant nestedness across taxonomic, functional and phylogenetic dimensions. The habitat-by-site matrix was also significantly nested. Spearman rank correlations between the selected predictors and nestedness ranks revealed that sky island area, climate stability and species traits associated with extinction vulnerability (minimum area requirement, larval stage duration, elevation range, and habitat specificity) were strongly correlated with taxonomic nestedness. Additionally, sky island area and climate stability significantly influenced functional and phylogenetic nestedness. These findings support the ‘selective extinction’ and ‘habitat nestedness’ hypotheses. To explain these results, we propose a climate stability hypothesis specific to sky islands: stable climatic conditions sustain greater species diversity, whereas climatic instability exacerbates the extinction of lineages lacking adaptive traits. This study presents the first empirical evidence of nestedness in sky island systems, extending classical hypotheses beyond lowland ecosystems and offering new insights into climate-driven assembly mechanisms affecting vulnerable taxa (e.g. amphibians). Our results indicate that conservation efforts should prioritize sky island regions with high-climate stability, large areas and diverse habitats as core areas for biodiversity protection. Moreover, species with narrow elevation ranges, large area requirements, high-habitat specificity and long larval stage durations should also be preserved to prevent local extinction.

摘要

嵌套分布格局是指物种较贫乏岛屿中的物种是物种较丰富岛屿中的物种的一个适当子集的物种分布格局，它常被用于解释岛屿和破碎化栖息地系统的物种分布。山地天空岛是理解地理隔离和气候变化所产生的进化后果的重要天然实验室，但是其物种分布格局及其影响因素尚不清楚。与低地破碎化栖息地岛屿相比，山地生物多样性格局更复杂，传统的驱动因素可能无法充分解释其群落的嵌套分布格局。 为了揭示山区生物多样性的形成原因，本研究在大别山地区对 30个天空岛的两栖动物进行了野外调查，旨在从物种、功能和系统发育三个方面，探索天空岛两栖类的嵌套分布格局及其形成机制。物种嵌套性通过构建物种关联矩阵并计算嵌套程度来衡量，而功能和系统发育嵌套性则通过结合物种在生态性状和系统发育方面的相似性来量化。为了解释嵌套分布格局，我们选取了7个天空岛特征和8个两栖类物种性状作为嵌套性的预测因子。 结果表明，大别山区两栖动物群落在物种、功能和系统发育三个方面均表现出显著的嵌套性。同时，栖息地分布矩阵也是显著嵌套的。将不同的预测因子与嵌套性进行斯皮尔曼相关分析，发现天空岛面积、气候稳定性和与灭绝相关的物种特征(最小面积需求、蝌蚪期长度、海拔分布范围、生境专属性)与物种嵌套性高度相关。此外，天空岛面积和气候稳定性显著影响功能和系统发育的嵌套性。因此，研究结果支持“选择性灭绝”和“栖息地嵌套性”假说。 在此基础上，我们提出了适用于天空岛的气候稳定性假说:稳定的气候环境可维持更多的物种种类，而气候不稳定则往往会加剧缺乏适应性特征谱系的物种灭绝。本研究首次提供了天空岛系统嵌套分布格局的实证证据，将经典假设扩展到低地系统之外，为嵌套分布格局研究提供了新的视角，完善了两栖类等脆弱类群的气候驱动群落聚集机制。 根据研究结果，在制定生物多样保护措施时，须优先把那些气候稳定性高、面积大和生境类型多的天空岛区域作为核心区域来开展保护工作。此外，还应优先保护那些最小面积需求大、蝌蚪期长、海拔分布范围窄、生境专属性高的物种，以防止它们发生局部灭绝。
